$description: Page & flow composition recipes for the ObserveOps design system. Each recipe is a product-faithful blueprint for assembling catalogued components into a whole screen/flow. `id`s + `variant`s reference components/index.json + the registries. This is the layer above per-component docs — it tells an AI HOW to lay out a page, not just which parts exist.
$howToUse: 1. Match the user's screen to a recipe by `whenToUse` / `examples`.
2. Build the `regions` top-to-bottom / outer-to-inner: each region names component `id`s + `variant`s — open those in components/registry/ for props.
3. Apply `layout.shell` + `layout.tokens` (resolve via tokens/variables.json + tokens/structural.json) for spacing/sizing.
5. The product content (which columns/fields/options) is domain data the DS does not own — fill from the user's spec.
6. A region marked `$gap` references a layer NOT catalogued in the DS yet — do NOT improvise it. STOP and ASK the user (see ../AGENTS.md deviation rule).

$knownGaps.$note: Charts, the topology graph and the dashboard widget-grid are catalogued as the `data-viz` GUIDE family (registry/data-viz.json), not as obs-* web components. Wherever a recipe region needs one: (1) pick the TYPE via data-viz decisionFlow, (2) colour from tokens/chart-palette.json, (3) render with the PRODUCT'S component in-repo — Chart (components/chart), Graph (monitor-graph), Widgets (components/widgets) — or STOP-and-ASK if standalone. The region still carries `$gap` to mark the app-coupled boundary.
$knownGaps.charts: Charts / stat tiles (line/bar/donut/gauge/heatmap/sparkline/topn/…): no obs-* — see registry/data-viz.json for the type + palette; render with the product Chart component (Highcharts). Standalone -> STOP and ASK.
$knownGaps.topologyGraph: The Cytoscape topology / node-graph canvas: no obs-* — see data-viz `topology-graph`; render with monitor-graph/graph.vue. Standalone -> STOP and ASK.
$knownGaps.widgetGrid: The dashboard widget-grid (resizable tiles, vue-grid-layout): no obs-* — see data-viz `widget-grid`; render with components/widgets. Standalone -> STOP and ASK.

layout.appShell: Every authenticated page sits inside the app shell: the Primary nav (navigation/primary-nav, left, 65px collapsed) + the App header (toolbars/app-header, top, @header-height 55px) come from the layout, not the page. A page renders inside the main content area (--common-main-bg).

gotchas: Row actions are the Menu/context-menu (FlotoGridActions) — its prop/event contract is in menu.json apis.ContextMenu; NOT a Dropdown picker.

recipes.name: Dashboard view
recipes.whenToUse: A canvas of data widgets for a monitoring overview — Alert Summary, NOC, infra health. Charts/gauges/heatmaps/metrics tiled in a grid, with a global time range and (optionally) a draggable timeline.
recipes.contract: dashboard — ALSO call get_page_contract('dashboard') for the canvas token, scroll ownership, sticky header + shadow-on-scroll, gutter/gap scale and mandatory components this recipe doesn't carry; run validate_page(html,'dashboard') when done.

regions.note: The dashboard renders INSIDE the app shell (module rail + app-header), not as a bare content area — see the module-screen recipe.

use.note: the dashboard title; full-width WITH a bottom border, title weight 500, end-to-end (no side padding, inset only via --page-header-padding).
the global time-range picker (size='lg'). The resolved date-range readout is a SEPARATE sibling beside it — NOT inside the picker.

regions.note: This whole header block is position:sticky with a grey shadow that appears only once content scrolls beneath it (get_page_contract dashboard).

use.note: kind='slider' — a draggable timeline over the window. LINK it to the range picker via range-start/range-end (feed the picker's change fromMs/toMs in). Follow it with a full-width obs-divider.

obs-widget-grid — the arrangeable 12-col canvas (drag/drop/resize + collision push-down + gravity compaction + edge auto-scroll; emits layout-change). For a STATIC board use a plain CSS grid instead (route-away).

obs-widget-card — the widget chrome (grey header: title + time badge + hover kebab Full Screen/Share/Edit/Clone/Remove; drag handle + resize grip). Every widget IS one of these; place each with data-x/data-y/data-w/data-h; its BODY goes in the default slot.

DS charts — there is NO obs-chart element; render the captured chart-library fixtures via the dsChart() helper (line/area/column/bar/stacked/multi-line/pie/donut…). Chart tooltip = the DS chart tooltip (colour swatch + name + bold value, mono font). Reflow each chart on card resize (Highcharts reflows on WIDTH only).
obs-gauge — a ring dial (arc=value/total, severity colour, mono 28px/600 centre number) for Monitor-Availability / Alert-Count.
obs-severity-heatmap — the severity honeycomb with a hover tooltip (IP + location + severity pill).
obs-metric-list / obs-key-value for metric tiles.

regions.note: The custom-engine anomaly / forecast / geo-map types are still DATA-ONLY gaps — call list_gaps and STOP and ASK for those.

use.note: obs-noc-player — auto-rotate dashboards on a wallboard; pausable + respects reduced-motion.

layout.shell: sticky header (title + time range + optional timeline) over a full-width obs-widget-grid; FLUSH (edge-to-edge, no page padding); body gutter 0 10px 10px.

gotchas: Canvas is --page-background-color (WHITE) — NOT --common-main-bg (the app grey). This is the #1 dashboard mistake.
Widgets are obs-widget-card — NOT a generic .card div and NOT obs-toolbar’s widget-header.
Arrangeable board = obs-widget-grid; static board = a plain CSS grid.
The date-range readout is a separate sibling, not part of the picker; link the picker ↔ timeline via range-start/range-end.
Charts reflow on WIDTH only — reflow them when a card resizes, or a taller card leaves empty space.
a11y: NOC/wallboard rotation must be pausable + respect reduced-motion.
Drag/resize is pointer-only today — provide a non-drag way to arrange for keyboard users if needed.

recipes.name: Module screen (full app-chrome page)
recipes.whenToUse: A COMPLETE product module screen — not just the content area. Start here when building a page from scratch: it composes the app chrome (module rail + app header + module title + tab row + optional section menu) AROUND a content region. Use this instead of a bare content page; the rail/header/tabs come from the shell, the content from an inner recipe (list-view / explorer-view / detail-view).

contains.note: the product 16 modules — COPY the canonical key/label/icon list from the sidebar registry `productModules.items` (get_component('sidebar')); do NOT pick icons by eye (e.g. Topology = 'topology' a node tree, NOT 'networkTopology' a switch). Set `active` to the current module. 65px collapsed, hover-expands as an OVERLAY. Ships the ObserveOps logo by default — keep it.
global search + notifications + account via slots — compose obs-command-palette / obs-notification-menu / obs-user-menu (the user menu also drives Dark/Light/Auto).

the module section/category rail (mode list/sections/tree). Flush white + right border; use its `logo` (header) + default (footer, e.g. + New Category) slots.
the actual content — usually one of the content recipes; list-view is the most common.
settings drawer (slide-over, actions slot for the footer) + confirm dialogs (obs-modal variant=confirm), top-layer.

recipes.layout: rail (fixed 65px, overlays on expand) | { app-header (top) / module-title / module-tabs / [ side-menu (optional left) | content ] }. Rail + header are the shell; title + tabs + side-menu + content stack inside the main area.
gotchas: A screen STARTS FROM THE APP SHELL, not a bare content page — build rail + header + title + tabs first, then drop a content recipe inside. A bare content page is a harness, not a screen.
Three different navs, do not conflate: between-MODULE = obs-sidebar (rail); sibling VIEWS of one module = obs-tabs; in-module SECTION/category = obs-side-menu.
The side-menu is optional — only modules with sub-sections/categories have one.
obs-layout-appshell renders but has no data contract (reference-only) — assemble these regions from the elements above rather than expecting one shell component.
recipes.a11y: One <main> for the content; the rail is <nav aria-label="Primary">, the side-menu another <nav>; the module tab row is a tablist. Do not nest multiple <main>.
recipes.contract: After picking the inner content recipe, call get_page_contract(pageType) — dashboard | list | settings | form — for the canvas token, scroll ownership, sticky/gutter rules the structure doesn't carry; validate_page(html, pageType) when done.
